source.author: A.C. Gibson
source.title: Vascular Plants of Williamson County: Maurandella antirrhiniflora subsp. antirrhiniflora
source.notes: Applies explicitly to the nominate subspecies and is a regional Texas descriptive treatment

name_crosswalk.accepted_species: Maurandella antirrhiniflora (Humb. & Bonpl. ex Willd.) Rothm.
name_crosswalk.historical_name: Maurandya antirrhiniflora Humb. & Bonpl. ex Willd.

source_reported_morphology.growth_habit: Perennial vine scrambling over plants and twining by petioles, branching from axillary buds
source_reported_morphology.stems: Cylindric, slender and usually glabrous, to 2 mm diameter
source_reported_morphology.leaves: Helically alternate, subopposite low on stem; often three-lobed, triangular-hastate or sagittate; blade (4.5–)6–27 × (4.5–)5–30 mm; long petioles to 19 mm, which may coil around support
source_reported_morphology.flowers: Solitary axillary, bilateral, flower approximately 15–18 mm across; two-lipped five-lobed corolla about 20 mm long, blue to violet-blue lobes and whitish to pale violet spotted throat
source_reported_morphology.capsule: Two-chambered globose dehiscent capsule ca. 5–6 × 5–6.5 mm, persistent angled style-derived beak ca. 2–3.3 mm
source_reported_morphology.seeds: Dull brown, ca. 1–1.3 × 0.8–1 mm with corky winglike coverings

limitations: Subspecies-level measurements should not be asserted for every different Maurandella taxonomic concept without checking scope.
